purpose: Aimovig is used to help prevent migraines in adults who get them frequently. It is not used to treat a migraine that has already started. By taking it regularly, many people have fewer migraines each month.
how_it_works: During a migraine, your body releases a protein called CGRP that causes pain and inflammation in your head. Aimovig is an antibody that blocks the receptor where CGRP attaches, like putting a lock on a door so the key cannot get in. This helps prevent migraines from starting in the first place.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are redness, pain, or itching at the injection site where you give yourself the shot. Some people also experience constipation, which can sometimes be severe. Muscle cramps or spasms have also been reported.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have serious constipation or bowel problems, as this medication can make constipation worse. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Some patients have had allergic reactions such as rash or swelling, so stop using it and call your doctor right away if that happens. Keep the autoinjector pen in the refrigerator and let it warm up at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before using it.
typical_dosing: Aimovig is given as a shot under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once a month. The usual dose is either 70 mg or 140 mg per month depending on what your doctor prescribes. It comes as an easy-to-use prefilled autoinjector pen that you can give yourself at home.
